title: A policy variable from a key with several values
question: What does AWS do with a policy variable whose key has several values? AWS says "You can't use a multivalued condition key as a variable", but not what happens if a policy does. The analyzer refuses.

cases.name: first_value
cases.description: A request on the bucket named after the first value.

cases.name: second_value
cases.description: A request on the bucket named after the second value.

cases.name: not_resource_on_a_value
cases.description: Second follow-up: a Deny on every bucket but the one ${aws:TagKeys} names, under an Allow for all of S3, on the bucket named after the first value.

readings.EXPLICIT_DENY: the variable's resource matches nothing, so NotResource covers every bucket, as with a variable that has no value
readings.ALLOW: the statement is dropped, or blue is used

cases.name: not_resource_on_another_bucket
cases.description: Second follow-up: the same Deny, on a bucket named after neither value.

readings.EXPLICIT_DENY: the variable's resource matches nothing, or a value is used; with not_resource_on_a_value, this tells them apart
